meta.vantage: github-hosted ubuntu runner to the ap-southeast-2 staging stack; budgets derived here are not comparable to numbers measured from any other vantage

readlist-switch-first.note: budgetMs was raised from 800 after CI run 37014635553 breached in both the measured batch (max 886ms) and the confirmation re-measure (max 900ms), so the tail is real rather than a hiccup. The control probe held near 215ms from start to end, and every slow sample spent its time between request and swap, so the tail is server side, not the runner. It replaces a 19-run soak baseline whose worst was 763ms. budgetMs is the 900ms worst rounded up to the next 50ms. Ratchet target once the listing cache lands — this is the cache-miss arm.

readlist-switch-subsequent.note: budgetMs was raised from 450 after CI run 37293064059 breached in both the measured batch (max 491ms) and the confirmation re-measure (max 498ms), so the tail is real rather than a hiccup. That run is the worst of the 84 post-deploy runs from 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-06 and the only one with a batch over 450ms. budgetMs is the 498ms worst rounded up to the next 50ms. It replaces a 19-run soak baseline whose worst was 406ms. Ratchet target once the listing cache lands — this is the cache-hit arm and should fall furthest.

tab-switch-first.note: budgetMs was raised from 450 after the 86 post-deploy runs from 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-06 put 10 measured batches over it and failed two deploys on the confirmation re-measure. The worst was CI run 36877368888, which breached in both the measured batch (max 627ms) and the confirmation (max 527ms). budgetMs is the 627ms worst rounded up to the next 50ms. It replaces a 19-run soak baseline whose worst was 414ms. Cache-miss arm of the To-Read/Read switch.

tab-switch-subsequent.note: budgetMs was raised from 400 to 450 after a 20-run soak measured 449ms for this operation, above the 400ms gate. That 449 was a lone outlier 68ms clear of the next worst — the other 19 runs spanned 257 to 381ms with a 332ms median max, and the operation's median max improved from 347 to 331 over the same soak — but the suite's confirmation re-measure reproduced it, so it is a real tail rather than a hiccup. Cache-hit arm of the To-Read/Read switch.

assign-to-readlist.note: budgetMs was raised from 750 after the 82 post-deploy runs from 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-06 put 6 measured batches over it and CI run 35851037775 failed a deploy on the confirmation re-measure (max 831ms). The worst batch was 847ms in CI run 37408286482, whose confirmation held at 700ms. budgetMs is the 847ms worst rounded up to the next 50ms. It replaces a 19-run soak baseline whose worst was 715ms. Ratchet target when the assign response becomes an out-of-band fragment instead of a full reader re-render.

open-article.note: The open is now a boosted same-document swap that paints a reader skeleton after 150ms and fills it asynchronously; the sample carries beforeRequest/afterSwap/afterSettle phases rather than a document hop. budgetMs was raised from 600 after CI run 36126192518 measured a 631ms batch, the worst of the 81 post-deploy runs from 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-06, all of them same-document opens. Its confirmation re-measure held at 431ms, so no deploy failed on this gate. budgetMs is the 631ms worst rounded up to the next 50ms. It replaces a 19-run soak baseline of new-document opens whose worst was 564ms.

back-to-readlist.note: budgetMs is baseline.maxMs rounded up to the next 50ms — 2.0% above the worst run the soak saw. That worst run is an outlier: 18 of the 19 landed between 327 and 489ms and the median max was 402ms. Ratchet target when the reader exit becomes instant.
